title: TP-Link Omada
desc: Business Wi-Fi, switches, gateways and cloud management from TP-Link

pages.t: Omada is TP-Link's business networking brand. Its site tagline is "Networks Empower Business". It covers gateways, switches, Wi-Fi access points and security cameras, all managed centrally.
g: Access point (AP)
A device that gives Wi-Fi coverage and connects by cable to the network.
Gateway
The device that connects the local network to the internet and enforces rules.

pages.t: Omada names these settings: offices, hotels, multi-dwelling units (apartment buildings), chain restaurants and stores, warehouses, and outdoor sites such as farms and parking lots. It also pitches 4G for remote locations.

The pitch is centralised management: see and configure all devices from one place, even across many sites. Omada also promotes a unified network and surveillance solution together with its sister brand VIGI (cameras).
g: Centralised management
Controlling many devices from one screen instead of logging into each one.

quiz.q: What is Omada?
o: A consumer Wi-Fi router for homes only
quiz.w: Omada is TP-Link's business networking line: gateways, switches, access points and cameras.

quiz.q: Which customer is named as a typical Omada setting?
o: A mobile phone operator's core network
A data centre with thousands of servers
quiz.w: Omada lists hotels, offices, apartment buildings, chain restaurants and stores, warehouses and outdoor sites.

quiz.q: What is the main idea behind Omada's design?
o: Every device is set up separately
Devices are managed centrally, even across many sites
quiz.w: Centralised management across sites is the core pitch.

pages.t: Gateways connect the site to the internet: wired, Wi-Fi, 4G/5G, integrated and DSL types, plus the Fusion and Fusion Pro series. Switches link the wired devices and range from easy-managed Agile models up to stackable Layer 3 campus switches, plus industrial ones.
g: Switch
A box that connects many wired devices in one network.
PoE
Power over Ethernet: power and data over one network cable.

pages.t: Access points come as ceiling, wall plate, desktop, outdoor and campus types, including Wi-Fi 7 models, plus wireless bridges. Cameras, video recorders and camera systems sit under the VIGI surveillance side.
g: Wireless bridge
A pair of radios linking two buildings or networks without a cable.

pages.t: Omada also sells accessories: power and PoE parts, media converters, modules and cables, and mounting brackets. Omada also lists a Design Hub among its software tools, and offers a unified networking and surveillance solution.

quiz.q: What does a gateway do?
o: Gives Wi-Fi coverage in a room
Connects the site to the internet
quiz.w: A gateway connects the local network to the internet and enforces rules.

quiz.q: Which is a listed Omada access point type?
quiz.w: Omada lists ceiling, wall plate, desktop, outdoor, campus and Wi-Fi 7 access points.

quiz.q: Where do Omada's cameras and recorders sit?
o: In the surveillance range alongside networking
quiz.w: Cameras, video recorders and camera systems are a category of their own, tied to VIGI.

lessons.title: Three ways to run the controller

pages.t: A controller is the software brain that manages all Omada devices together. Omada offers three kinds: cloud-based, hardware and software. Choosing one is often the first decision in a project.
g: Controller
Software that configures and monitors many network devices from one place.

pages.t: A hardware controller is a small box on site: OC200, OC220, OC300 or OC400, in growing sizes. The software controller is free, runs on the customer's own server or VM and needs someone to keep it running and updated.
g: VM
Virtual machine: a computer simulated inside another computer.

pages.t: The cloud-based controller is hosted by Omada, so no box or server is needed on site. The trade-off: management depends on internet access. Hardware and software controllers can also add optional cloud access for remote management.

quiz.q: A customer has no IT staff and no server. Which controller option removes the need for any on-site controller?
quiz.w: The cloud-based controller is hosted by Omada, so nothing is installed on site.

quiz.q: Which statement about the software controller is right?
o: It runs on the customer's own server or VM and must be maintained
It is a small box powered by PoE
quiz.w: The customer provides and maintains the host, including uptime, updates and backups.

quiz.q: Which is an Omada hardware controller?
quiz.w: OC200, OC220, OC300 and OC400 are hardware controllers. ER7206 is a gateway.

quiz.q: What is the trade-off of cloud management?
quiz.w: Cloud management needs a reliable internet connection, but Omada looks after the platform.

pages.t: Omada Central Essentials is a free, simplified cloud tier for Omada and VIGI devices. Omada describes lifetime free cloud management for small businesses such as hostels, small offices and restaurants.
g: Tier
A level of a service, for example a free basic one and a paid fuller one.

pages.t: The Standard tier adds features Essentials lacks, such as MSP mode, PPSK, SD-WAN, more VPN types, 802.1X and IDS/IPS. Omada states that Standard carries a device licence fee, and lists Essentials as free.
g: MSP mode
A view for service providers managing many separate customers.
Licence fee
A charge to use a feature, here per device.

pages.t: Small, simple sites can start on Essentials. Larger, spread-out or multi-customer networks point to Standard. Always check the current licence terms with the vendor before quoting, and never promise features from memory.

quiz.q: A small restaurant wants easy, free cloud management of its Wi-Fi. Which fits?
quiz.w: Essentials is the free cloud tier aimed at small sites such as restaurants and hostels.

quiz.q: An MSP wants one view of many separate customer networks. What is needed?
o: A Standard tier with MSP mode
quiz.w: MSP mode is a Standard feature and is not in Essentials.

quiz.q: What does Omada say about licence fees?
o: Standard has a device licence fee, Essentials is free
quiz.w: Standard is subject to a device licence fee. Essentials is listed as free.

pages.t: The wired ER7206 is an Omada VPN gateway. It lists load balancing across up to five internet lines, failover, and support for several VPN types. It runs under a controller, or standalone through its own web page.
g: Load balancing
Spreading traffic over several internet lines.
VPN
A secure tunnel between sites or to a remote user.

pages.t: PPSK gives every unit its own Wi-Fi password and its own VLAN, so tenants stay separated on one network. Omada's PPSK pitch is apartments, student housing and assisted living. Its hotel page does not describe PPSK, so check before promising it for hotels.
g: PPSK
Private Pre-Shared Key: a unique Wi-Fi password per user or room.
VLAN
A virtual split of one network into separate private parts.

pages.t: Large properties can add an external RADIUS server to handle very many PPSK entries. Smaller ones can host PPSKs on the APs through the software controller. In the cloud, PPSK is a Standard feature, not in free Essentials.
g: RADIUS
A server that checks who is allowed onto the network.

quiz.q: What does PPSK give an apartment building?
o: A unique Wi-Fi password and VLAN per unit
quiz.w: PPSK means each unit has its own password and its own separated VLAN.

quiz.q: A customer has two internet lines and wants them used together. Which gateway feature matters?
quiz.w: Load balancing spreads traffic across several internet lines. The ER7206 lists up to five.

quiz.q: Which cloud tier includes PPSK?
quiz.w: Omada's tier comparison lists PPSK as missing in Essentials.

lessons.title: Which Omada setup for which customer?

pages.t: Omada's own guide: Essentials for small simple sites, a hardware controller for sites wanting local control and offline management, the software controller for medium to large networks, and Standard cloud for large or multi-customer setups.

Rivals such as UniFi also offer on-site consoles and a cloud view. A point to stress for Omada is choice: cloud, box or your own server. UniFi markets itself as licence free. Check current terms on both sides before comparing.
g: UniFi
Ubiquiti's networking line, a common alternative for small business.

pages.t: How many sites? Is there IT staff and a server? Is internet always reliable? Does the site need hotel or tenant Wi-Fi with PPSK? Are cameras part of the project? The answers decide controller type and tier.

quiz.q: A chain of 30 small shops wants remote, multi-store management. What should you start with?
o: Cloud management, checking Essentials against Standard
A single hardware OC200 per store with no remote access
quiz.w: Omada lists chain stores as a target setting and pitches central management across sites. The tier depends on the features needed.

quiz.q: A factory site often loses internet but wants local control. Which controller fits best?
quiz.w: Omada lists the hardware controller for sites wanting local control and offline management.

quiz.q: An IT-capable customer wants full control on its own server. Which?
quiz.w: The software controller runs on the customer's own server or VM, with the most control and most IT work.

quiz.q: What is a fair way to describe Omada versus UniFi?
o: Omada offers a choice of cloud, hardware or software control
quiz.w: Controller choice is a real difference. Never claim price or feature superiority without checking.
